text:
Want Osaka without the tour groups? These are the two neighbourhoods we'd pick for a second trip. 🏮

📍 Tenma — one stop from Osaka Station on the JR Loop Line. Tenjinbashisuji, Japan's longest covered shopping street (2.6 km, about 600 shops), runs right through it. At night the lantern-lit alleys just north of JR Tenma, known as Ura-Tenma, fill up with office workers and neighbours rather than tour groups.

📍 Tsuruhashi — Osaka's Korean neighbourhood. The market lanes start right outside the station, and Miyuki-dori Koreatown is a 10–15 minute walk south. JR, Kintetsu and the Metro all stop here, including Kintetsu trains straight to Nara.

Our take: on a first trip with two or three nights, stay central. On a second trip, for four nights or more, or if food is the main reason you're going, Tenma or Tsuruhashi gives you everyday Osaka.

Full guide with lines and walking times 👉 https://japanbystation.com/osaka-live-like-a-local
